This Day, The Court Pronounced The Following:
 Judgment
Appellant owner of offending vehicle challenged the judgment and award passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT, T.Narasipura, in MVC No.38/2013, dated 01.09.2016.

sentences.text: 2. Parties are referred with their ranks as assigned in the Trial Court for the sake of convenience.

3. The factual matrix leading to the case of claimant can be stated in nutshell to the effect that on 25.11.2012 at 12.45 p.m., the claimant was proceeding on his Bajaj Discovery bike bearing No.KA 55 K 0952 on Mysore- T.Narasipura road near Keelanapura.
At that time, driver of Maruthi Suzuki car bearing No.KA 09 M 6195 came from opposite side and dashed against front side of motorcycle.

Due to which, claimant sustained injuries, he was admitted to Cauvery Hospital, Siddharthnagar Mysore,
and took treatment in the said hospital from 25.11.2012 to 07.12.2012.
The claimant has undergone surgery and spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for treatment.

On account of accidental injuries,
claimant has suffered permanent disability and unable to do the work as he was to do earlier.
Therefore, prayed for grant of compensation.
4. In response to the notice, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 have appeared through counsel and filed separate written statement.
Respondent No.1-driver of offending vehicle contended that accident occurred due to contributory negligence of claimant who was under intoxication.

Respondent No.2-owner of the vehicle contended that he was registered owner of Maruthi Suzuki car No.KA 09 M 6195 and he has sold the said vehicle to one Sri John s/o Kiritappa on 13.09.2007 and delivered possession of vehicle to the purchaser on obtaining delivery note.
Therefore, respondent No.2 was not the owner of offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
The purchaser of vehicle has sold the same to one Mehaboob Pasha owner of Friends Auto Consultancy with all relevant records of the vehicle.
Therefore, the subsequent purchaser K John and Mehaboob Pasha are necessary parties to the claim petition and without impleading them as parties, the claim petition itself is not maintainable.
On these grounds, both respondents sought for dismissal of claim petition.
5. The claimant in order to prove his case relied on evidence of PW.1 and documents Exs.P.1 to P.10.
Respondent No.2 relied on evidence of RWs.1 and 2 and documents at Ex.R.1.
Court Commissioner is examined as CW.1 and Exs.C.1 to C.8 came to be marked.

The Tribunal after hearing both sides Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155220184/
2 and on appreciation of evidence on record has allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of Rs.5,21,779/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire amount.

The liability to pay compensation was fixed on respondent Nos.1 and 2.
6.
Respondent No.2 owner of offending vehicle challenged the judgment and award fixing liability to pay the compensation.

It is contended that the Tribunal has completely ignored evidence of RWs.1 and 2 with Ex.R.1 and erroneously recorded finding that respondent No.2 is still owner of vehicle as on the date of accident.
The document Ex.R.1 delivery note and admission of RW.2 that he has purchased the offending vehicle from respondent No.2 has not been properly appreciated by the Tribunal.
The Tribunal has also failed to appreciate the law laid down by this Court in H D Chandrappa vs. Hanumakka and others reported in 2014 ACJ page No.402.

entities.text: H D Chandrappa vs. Hanumakka and others reported in 2014 ACJ page No.402
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The approach and appreciation of evidence by Tribunal is contrary to law and evidence on record.
Therefore, prayed for allowing the appeal and to set aside the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.
7. In response to notice of appeal, respondents have appeared through their respective counsel.

8. Heard the argument of both sides.
9.

The claimant contended that accident occurred on 25.11.2012 on Mysore-T.Narasipura road while he was proceeding on Bajaj Discovery bike bearing No.KA 55 K 0952, the driver of Maruthi Suzuki Car bearing No. KA 09 M 6195 came from opposite side in rash and negligent manner dashed against front side of the motorcycle.
Due to which, the claimant sustained accidental injuries.

The Tribunal on appreciating the evidence of PW.1 and documents Ex.P.1-FIR and complaint,
Ex.P.2-spot mahazar, Ex.P.3 rough sketch, Ex.P.4 IMV report, Ex.P.5 charge sheet and Ex.P.6 wound certificate recorded finding that accident in question has occurred due to actionable negligence of the driver of Maruthi Suzuki car bearing No.KA 09 M 6195.
The respondent No.1-driver of the offending vehicle

though contended that accident has occurred due to contributory negligence of rider of motorcycle who was under intoxication has neither cross- examined PW.1 nor led his evidence to prove the said fact.
Therefore, Tribunal was justified in holding that accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
10. The quantum of compensation awarded by Tribunal is not under challenge by the claimant.
It is only the owner of offending vehicle respondent No.2 challenged the judgment and award of Tribunal in fixing liability on respondent Nos.1 and 2 to pay the compensation amount with interest.
11. Learned counsel for appellant has argued that respondent No.2 was not the owner of offending vehicle as on the date of accident.
The evidence of RW.2 and delivery note Ex.R.1 would speak about the sale of offending vehicle on 13.09.2007 much prior to accident.
The said fact has been admitted by RW.2 who is purchaser of offending vehicle from respondent No.2.
The Tribunal has conveniently ignored the said material on record and committed serious error in fastening liability on respondent Nos.1 and 2 to pay compensation.

Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155220184/
3 12.

entities.text: Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for claimant has argued that the name of respondent No.2 is still continued as owner of vehicle in the records of RTO and therefore, the owner is liable to pay the compensation.

The evidence of RW.2 and delivery note Ex.R.1 is accepted for the sake of argument regarding transfer of offending vehicle much prior to the accident then also appellant cannot be absolved from the liability to pay compensation.
13. The respondent No.1 driver of offending vehicle in the written statement did not disclose the name of owner of offending vehicle.
Respondent No.1 also has not cross- examined PW.1 regarding the ownership of the offending vehicle.
Indisputably the charge sheet is filed against respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2 was admittedly owner of Maruthi Suzuki Car bearing No KA 09 M 6195 and his name was recorded in the records of the vehicle as owner.
It is the contention of respondent No.2 that he has sold the vehicle to one K John on 13.09.2007 and delivered possession of vehicle with delivery note as per Ex.R.1.
Therefore, respondent No.2 being not the owner in possession and control of the vehicle, he is not liable to pay compensation.
14. The evidence of Rws.1 and 2 would go to show that respondent No.2 has sold the offending vehicle on 13.09.2007 to one K John on obtaining delivery note as per Ex.R.1.
Thereafter, the purchaser K john has sold the said vehicle in favour of Mehaboob Pasha and executed necessary documents in his favour for transfer of the vehicle.
Indisputably, the offending vehicle was not insured as on the date of accident.
The question is as to whether who is owner of offending vehicle as on the date of accident and liability to pay compensation.

15. In view of Section 2(30) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'Act'), the term owner is defined as follows;
"2(30) "Owner" means, a person in whose name a motor vehicle stands registered,
and where such person is a minor, the guardian of such minor, and in relation to a motor vehicle which is the subject of a hire purchase agreement or an agreement of lease or an agreement of hypothecation, the person in whose possession of the vehicle under that agreement."
16.
The purpose of fixing such liability, the concept of ownership has to be understood in terms of above referred definition of owner under Section 2(30) of the Act.
In the present case, there are multifarious transactions relating to offending vehicle.
However, despite of that, the transferee did not get transfer of records of the vehicle, in terms of Section 50 of the Act.
Whenever there is transfer of motor vehicle, then Section 50 of the Act mandates that the transfer of a vehicle ought to be registered within 30 days of the sale.
Section 50(1) of the Act obliges the transferor to report the fact of transfer within 14 days of transfer.
In case the vehicle is sold outside the State, the period within which the transfer ought to be reported gets extended.

On the other hand, the transferee is also obliged to report the transfer to the Registering authority within whose jurisdiction the transferee has the residence or place of business where the vehicle is normally kept.
Thus, Section 50 of the Act prescribes timelines within which the transferor and the transferee are required to report the factum of transfer.

As per Sub-Section(3) of Section 50 of Act, if there be failure to report the fact of transfer, fine could be imposed and an action under Section 177 could thereafter be taken Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155220184/
4 if there is failure to pay the amount of fine.
These timelines and obligations are only to facilitate the reporting of the transfer.
It is not as if that if an accident occurs within the period prescribed for reporting said transfer, the transferor is absolved of the liability.
The obligation to report transfer of vehicle in terms of Section 50 is both on the transferor and the transferee.

17. Learned counsel for appellant in support of his contention that when RW.2 admits he has purchased offending vehicle from the appellant and execution of delivery note Ex.R.1, then in that event of the matter, appellant has to be exonerated from the liability to pay compensation relied on the judgment of this Court in H D Chandrappa's case referred above having considered the legal position in para 31 has held as under;
"Therefore, the emerging legal position would be in a case where the vehicle is not covered by a policy of insurance and a claim petition arising out of an accident involving such vehicle, if the person claimed as registered owner of the vehicle in the concerned register of the registering authority contends that he cease to be the owner of the vehicle on account of its sale, it is for him to show and establish that he cease to be owner, notwithstanding the fact that the registration certificate is not changed into the name of the transferee, and if he succeeds in doing so, then he will not be liable to answer the claim.
If he fails to do so, he would be liable to answer the claim of third parties."
The transferee is held to be liable to pay compensation, when the transferor establishes sale of vehicle and delivery of possession of vehicle as on the date of accident.
18. The above referred judgment has also been cited before the Tribunal.

However, the Tribunal by taking note of the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Dr. T V Jose vs. has held that in view of non-compliance of Section 50 of the Act and name of transferor being continued in the records of the vehicle has held that the transferor and the driver of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

19. Learned counsel for claimant relied on the judgment reported in AIR 2018 SC Page No.983,
Naveen Kumar vs. Vijay Kumar and others.

entities.text: Naveen Kumar vs. Vijay Kumar and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court by taking note of the judgment of Dr. T V Jose referred above, though was rendered under Motor Vehicles Act, 1939, the Court in Pushpa @ Leela Vs. Shankuntala, (2011) 2 SCC Page No.240, has held that the ratio of judgment "shall apply with equal force to the facts of the cases arising under the 1988 Act" in view of the provisions of Sections 2(30) and 50.

entities.text: Pushpa @ Leela Vs. Shankuntala, (2011) 2 SCC Page No.240
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Consequently, the view of this Court was that the person whose name continues in the record of the registering authority as the owner of the said vehicle is equally liable together with the insurer.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in para 12 of the judgment has held as under;
"The consistent thread of reasoning which emerges from the above decisions is that in view of the definition of the expression 'owner' in Section 2(30), it is the person in whose name the motor vehicle stands registered who, for the purpose of the act would be treated as the owner.

However, where a person is a minor, the guardian of Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155220184/
5 minor would be treated as the owner.

entities.text: Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Where the motor vehicle is subjected to agreement of hire purchase, lease of hypothecation, the person in possession of the vehicle under that agreement is treated as the owner.

In a situation such as the present where the registered owner has purported to transfer the vehicle but continues to be reflected in the records of the registering authority as the owner of the vehicle he would not stand absolved of liability.
Parliament has consciously introduced the definition of the expression 'owner' in Section 2(30), making a departure from the provisions of Section 2(19) in the earlier 1939 Act.

The principle underlying the provisions of Section 2(30) is that the victim of a motor accident or, in the case of death the legal heirs of deceased victim should not be left in a state of uncertainty.
A claimant for compensation ought not to be burdened with the following trail of successive transfers, which are not registered with the registering authority.
To hold otherwise would be defeat the salutary object and purpose of the Act.
Hence, the interpretation to be placed must facilitate the fulfillment of the object of the law.
In the present case, the first respondent was the 'owner' of the vehicle involved in the accident within the meaning of Section 2(30).
The liability to pay compensation stands fastened upon him."

entities.text: Prakash Chand Daga vs. Savita Sharma and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely because the vehicle was transferred does not mean that such registered owner stands absolved of his liability to a third person.
So long as his name continues in RTO records, he remains liable to a third person."
In the present case also the name of appellant still continues in the records of RTO as the registered owner of offending vehicle despite multifarious transfer of vehicle as on the date of accident.
The transferor or transferee did not make any effort to comply the mandate of law in terms of Section 50 of the Act.

Therefore, in view of the principles enunciated by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Naveen Kumar and Prakash Chand Daga, the appellant-respondent No.2 who was owner of the vehicle as on the date of accident has to pay compensation.

20. In light of above referred judgments, the contention of learned counsel for appellant that he was not the owner of offending vehicle as on the date of accident is not liable to pay compensation cannot be legally sustained.

On the basis of evidence of RW.2, if at all the appellant wish to make any claim against him for recovery of compensation amount arising out of dispute between the appellant and RW.2, then it is open for appellant to take recourse under law.
21. The Tribunal has held that respondent Nos.1 and 2 being driver and owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount.

In view of the reasons recorded as above, this Court has affirmed the finding of the Tribunal holding that respondent No.2 is the Sri. Jekab Philip vs Sri. Mahadevaswamy on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155220184/
6 owner of offending vehicle as on the date of accident and the accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of driver of Maruthi Suzuki car bearing No.KA 09 M 6195.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Tribunal has rightly appreciated the evidence on record and was justified in fastening the liability to pay compensation on respondent Nos.1 and 2 and the same does not call for interference by this Court.

Consequently, proceed to pass the following:
Order The appeal filed by the appellant/respondent No.2 is hereby dismissed.
The judgment and award passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT, T.Narasipura, in MVC No.38/2013, dated 01.09.2016 is hereby confirmed.
The amount deposited by appellant before this Court is ordered to be transferred to Tribunal.
Registry shall send a copy of this judgment along with records to Tribunal.
